summary: Grant County, OR lookout site in Malheur NF: 1934 L-4 cab, a 1937 garage plan, a 1953 staffing mention, cab removed or destroyed in 1971; no source found describing the site today.

facts.status_note: Cab removed (FFLOS) or destroyed (firelookout.com) in 1971; no source describes what remains today

staffing.status: staffed (July 1953 newspaper item names a lookout there)

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Malheur National Forest

events.note: Whitman Forest asked on August 2, 1937 for approval of standard one-car garage and storeroom plan 4-0-9; approved for this site August 6, 1937
Roger Stephen on lookout duty, per July 1953 Nyssa Gate City Journal item
FFLOS says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed
Registered June 13, 2011 as US 1058, OR 416; nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: built in 1934 as an L-4 cab, removed in 1971
evidence.quote: Built in 1934, this L-4 cab was removed in 1971.

evidence.supports: about 24 miles north-northeast of John Day
administered by the U.S. Forest Service

evidence.quote: August 2, 1937: Reference is made to attached Form R6-01 from the Whitman Forest requesting approval of plan 4-0-9

evidence.supports: approved for this site on August 6, 1937
evidence.quote: August 6, 1937: The one car garage and storage room for lookouts is approved for this site.

evidence.supports: July 1953 visit to Roger Stephen on a lookout
evidence.quote: Roger Stephen, who is on a lookout there

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says the L-4 cab was removed in 1971. Firelookout.com says destroyed in 1971. The sources agree on the year and differ on how the cab left the site. The story reports both words.

sources.title: Crockett Knob Lookout Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites (Forest Fire Lookout Association)

notes_for_editor: The brief has no access record and none was found; the access key is omitted rather than guessed. A 2022 Facebook post by the Northwest Coordination Center mentions a lookout built in 1957, but it refers to Indian Rock Lookout, not Crockett Knob, so it is not used. A geocaching listing for the site could not be read by the fetch tool. No source describes what remains at the site today. The 1937 and 1953 items are excerpts as printed on the Oregon Lookouts page; the original newspapers and files were not checked.
